subject: Re: Distinguishing Direct vs Ancillary Damages — drafting examples
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmepay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme - MSA redline: damages and caps

Hi Mina,

Thanks for sending the MSA. Our legal team has flagged the damages section — specifically the proposed carve-outs for lost profits and loss of goodwill. Acme’s position is that exclusion of consequential/indirect damages should be broad and that any carve-outs need to be narrowly tailored.

Two immediate asks from our side:
- Can you provide concrete drafting examples that draw a clear line between "direct" damages and "indirect/consequential" damages? We're especially worried about language that could allow lost profits and loss of goodwill claims to circumvent a cap.
- If you propose carve-outs for data loss or security incidents, please provide sample language and a suggested monetary treatment (e.g., separate cap, per-incident cap, or a higher overall cap).

I attached our redline (Acme_MSA_redline_v3.pdf). Can your team propose 2–3 discrete drafting options we can circulate internally?

Regards,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Legal Operations
Acme Payments

Attachment: Acme_MSA_redline_v3.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Acme - MSA redline: damages and caps

Tom — thanks for the note and the redline. We hear the concern; happy to propose concrete drafting options. High-level framing we use internally:

1) "Direct" damages = measurable out-of-pocket losses directly caused by a breach of the agreement (cost to remediate, replacement services, etc.).
2) "Indirect/Consequential" damages = downstream business harms like lost profits, loss of goodwill, or third-party fines.

Below are three drafting options (summarized). I included a separate doc with examples and clause text (Direct_vs_Indirect_Examples.docx).

Option A — Narrow carve-out: Allow recovery for data restoration and investigation costs as direct damages; exclude lost profits and goodwill. Cap remains the standard MSA cap (fees paid in prior 12 months).

Option B — Categorized carve-out (recommended):
- Maintain main cap (fees paid in prior 12 months) for general claims.
- Create a narrowly defined carve-out for: (i) proven, documented costs to restore or replace Customer data; (ii) reasonable third-party forensic costs; and (iii) regulatory fines where Redwood is directly liable (subject to indemnity rules).
- Lost profits and loss of goodwill remain excluded from recoverable damages.

Option C — Elevated cap for specific incidents: For security/data incidents that meet defined severity triggers, apply a separate per-incident cap (e.g., 3x quarterly fees or $XMM). Lost profits still excluded.

Next steps: I can upload the three redline snippets into the MSA and we can join a short call to walk Acme legal through the trade-offs. Do you have a target stakeholder (procurement / finance) we should bring in for the cap discussion?

Best,
Mina
Director, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Direct_vs_Indirect_Examples.docx

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmepay.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Legal Team <legal@acmepay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - MSA redline: damages and caps

Mina — appreciate the clear options. A couple of points from our side after internal review:

- We're unwilling to accept a carve-out that would, in effect, permit recovery of "lost profits" under another label. Any language that ties recovery to subjective "harm to business operations" will be problematic.
- If you insist on a carve-out for data restoration, Acme would prefer a single, modest per-incident cap tied to the Order Form (e.g., $500k per incident) rather than a multiplier of fees. That gives procurement predictable exposure.
- On forensic costs: fine if limited to documented third-party costs.

Would Redwood consider Option B but with two modifications: (1) explicit blacklist of categories ("lost profits", "loss of goodwill", "punitive/treble damages") and (2) per-incident cap for data restoration at $500k (we can negotiate the number).

We can loop in Procurement if you share an initial redline we can circulate in the Acme review queue.

Thanks,
Tom

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmepay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - MSA redline: damages and caps

Tom — thanks, that's helpful and gets us close. I've inlined a concise redline below and attached the doc with three clean clause variants for your legal team to circulate. My recommended path is Option B with the two tweaks you propose (explicit exclusions + per-incident cap for data restoration), but with a slightly higher demonstration cap to account for large enterprise restorations. Suggested language excerpt (inline redline):

-- Proposed new subsection (example) --
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following shall be treated as recoverable direct damages to the extent they are proven with reasonable documentation: (a) documented and reasonable third-party costs for forensic investigation and remediation of a security incident; (b) documented costs to restore or replace Customer Data corrupted or lost as a direct result of Redwood's breach, subject to a per-incident cap of $750,000 unless otherwise stated in the Order Form; and (c) reasonable third-party costs incurred to comply with notification requirements to affected individuals or regulators.
For clarity, "Direct Damages" does not include: lost profits, loss of business or goodwill, consequential, incidental, special, punitive, or exemplary damages, or other similar categories."

Notes:
- We kept lost profits and loss of goodwill expressly excluded.
- Per-incident cap: I proposed $750k but can change to $500k if Procurement pushes back — please advise.
- If Acme wants a sliding scale tied to ARR or Order Form value, we can draft an Order Form field: "Per-Incident Data Cap: $_____."

Laura / Marcus — can you take a quick look at the proposed language and flag any internal constraints (procurement, finance, or legal) that would make $750k untenable? If Procurement wants $500k, recommend we keep an exception that allows a higher negotiated per-incident cap in the Order Form for large enterprise customers.

Tom — I'll upload the redline into the shared Drive and send a DocuSign-ready MSA snippet if that helps move this to procurement review.

Best regards,
Mina
Director, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
